exposure: Low Pregnancy-associated plasma protein A (PAPP-A) in the first trimester
outcome: Newborn condition at delivery (Apgar score, birth weight)
finding: While low first-trimester PAPP-A was associated with a higher frequency of complications like premature birth and preeclampsia, it did not significantly affect newborn outcomes like Apgar score and birth weight.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section was similar between the low PAPP-A group (29.7%) and the control group (32%).
birth_weight: Birth weight data was collected, and birth weight under 2500g was more common in the low PAPP-A group, although this difference was not statistically significant.
